claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was Patriarch of Antioch from 324 to 330.
He was a native of Side in Pamphylia.
About 320 he was bishop of Beroea, and he became patriarch of Antioch shortly before the Council of Nicaea in 325.
Most of the numerous dogmatic and exegetical treatises of Eustathius have been lost.
The fragments survive from lost writings and are found in editions by Fabricius, Galland, Harles, Migne, Pitra, Martin, and others.
The fragments were edited in the eighteenth century by Johann Albrecht Fabricius and André Galland, with a revised edition by Gottlieb Harles in 1804.
J.P. Migne published a complete edition in PG 161, Paris 1857, 676-697.
In 1883, J.P. Paulin Martin published ten Syriac fragments attributed to Eustathius, with a Latin translation.
Jean Baptiste Pitra offered three further Greek fragments in 1884, previously unattributed to Eustathius.
The modern critical edition is by J.H. Declerck in Eustathii Antiocheni, patris Nicaeni, opera quae supersunt omnia, CCG 51, Turnhout 2002.

Eustathius distinguished himself zealously against the Arians at the Council of Nicaea, and he and Marcellus joined forces with Alexander to significantly influence the formulation of the Nicene Creed.
